Why this moment

The silicon shift.

Modern on-device compute, especially unified-memory systems, makes it practical to run large open-weight models locally for many real business workflows.

The regulatory wave.

The EU AI Act enters broad application in August 2026 with staged obligations. Documented workflows increase, and proprietary context matters.

The subscription ceiling.

Per-seat SaaS economics break when work becomes autonomous. Agents reduce seat counts and vendor exposure over time.

Departments, not tools

Command

Synthesizes priorities, surfaces what matters, drafts decision briefs. Your operational nerve center.

Analysis

Monitors markets, digests research, scans competitors. Produces intelligence, not data dumps.

Voice

Maintains tone consistency across every channel. Drafts, edits, and aligns communications at brand-level quality.

Growth

Builds campaign architectures, generates content systems, maps distribution. Strategy and execution in one loop.

Build

Structures web pages, iterates UX, proposes design improvements. Designed to ship, not just suggest.

Process

Captures procedures, maintains documentation, handles interdepartmental handoffs. Institutional memory that stays usable.

Environments

Where the node runs

Four deployment shapes, one operating model.

On-prem

A dedicated node in your own rack, off the public internet by default.

Colocation

Managed hardware in a nearby facility with a private link back to you.

Edge

Compact units placed close to where the work and the data already live.

Hybrid

Controlled pathways to frontier models when a task genuinely needs them.

One machine, an entire layer

Not a per-seat SaaS. A physical AI node you own, provisioned and yours.

  • ▪

Questions

Is my data sent anywhere?

No. The node is telemetry-minimal and stays off the public internet by default.

What happens when a model improves?

You update the node on your schedule; nothing about your data changes.

Can it reach frontier models?

Only through controlled, opt-in pathways you configure explicitly.
